newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND WINS WORLD CUP OVERALL CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND WINS WORLD CUP OVERALL CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Luc Alphand of France won the overall World Cup championship on Sunday at the World Cup Finals.

Alphand, who led Andre Kjetil Aamodt of Norway by 70 points going into the season's final race, claimed the championship when Aamodt failed to finish at least second in the climactic slalom race down Vail Mountain.
The 31-year-old Alphand became the first Frenchman since the great Jean-Claude Killy in 1968 to win the overall, and is the first speed specialist ever to claim the crown.

Aamodt, only 16th fastest after the first run, pushed into the lead with a combined time of 1:39.01 seconds. His lead lasted five skiers until giant slalom champion Michael von Gruenigen overtook him at 1:38.90.

The Norwegian clung desperately to a chance for second place through three more skiers until Mario Reiter of Austria, the 15th of 21 starters, dropped Aamodt down to third with a combined time of 1:38.49.
The race was won by Finn Christian Jagge of Norway in 1:37.94. Aamodt finished seventh.
Alphand watched the drama from the sidelines. The Frenchman races in only the downhill and Super-G events and ignores the technical races -- giant slalom and slalom.
The Frenchman also won the season title in both his specialities, winning four downhills and two Super-Gs this season.
